scope: Evening short-wavelength/melanopic-light filtering eyewear; excludes red-light therapy and photobiomodulation.

records.title: Efficacy of blue-light blocking glasses on actigraphic sleep outcomes: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled crossover trials
records.citation: Luna-Rangel FA, et al. Efficacy of blue-light blocking glasses on actigraphic sleep outcomes. Front Neurol. 2025;16:1699303. doi:10.3389/fneur.2025.1699303.
records.protocolTakeaway: Use to keep the protocol framed as a bounded self-experiment, not a reliable insomnia treatment.

records.title: Optimizing the Potential Utility of Blue-Blocking Glasses for Sleep and Circadian Health
records.citation: Glickman GL, et al. Optimizing the Potential Utility of Blue-Blocking Glasses for Sleep and Circadian Health. Transl Vis Sci Technol. 2025;14(7):25. doi:10.1167/tvst.14.7.25.
records.protocolTakeaway: Use as the product-quality guardrail and avoid brand recommendations unless spectral data is available.

records.title: Interventions to reduce short-wavelength (“blue”) light exposure at night and their effects on sleep: a systematic review and meta-analysis
records.citation: Shechter A, et al. Interventions to reduce short-wavelength (“blue”) light exposure at night and their effects on sleep. Sleep Adv. 2020;1(1):zpaa002. doi:10.1093/sleepadvances/zpaa002.
records.protocolTakeaway: Do not merge glasses, screen filters, and room-light dimming into one causal claim.

records.title: Evening wear of blue-blocking glasses for sleep and mood disorders: a systematic review
records.citation: Hester L, et al. Evening wear of blue-blocking glasses for sleep and mood disorders: a systematic review. Chronobiol Int. 2021;38(10):1375-1383. doi:10.1080/07420528.2021.1930029.
records.protocolTakeaway: Use as context-only evidence; split mood-disorder and circadian-disorder variants.

records.title: Blue-light filtering spectacle lenses for visual performance, sleep, and macular health in adults
records.citation: Singh S, et al. Blue-light filtering spectacle lenses for visual performance, sleep, and macular health in adults. Cochrane Database Syst Rev. 2023;8:CD013244. doi:10.1002/14651858.CD013244.pub2.
records.protocolTakeaway: Do not present this protocol as eye care or retinal protection.

records.title: Recommendations for daytime, evening, and nighttime indoor light exposure to best support physiology, sleep, and wakefulness in healthy adults
records.citation: Brown TM, et al. Recommendations for daytime, evening, and nighttime indoor light exposure to best support physiology, sleep, and wakefulness in healthy adults. PLoS Biol. 2022;20(3):e3001571. doi:10.1371/journal.pbio.3001571.
records.protocolTakeaway: Use glasses as one possible evening-light tool, not an all-day blue-light avoidance rule.

records.title: Light for Public Health Consensus Statements
records.citation: Light for Public Health Consortium. Light for Public Health Consensus Statements. doi:10.17617/1.4a6s-ec74.
records.protocolTakeaway: Keep the intervention in the evening window and preserve daytime light.

records.title: Blocking nocturnal blue light for insomnia: A randomized controlled trial
records.citation: Shechter A, et al. Blocking nocturnal blue light for insomnia: A randomized controlled trial. J Psychiatr Res. 2018;96:196-202. doi:10.1016/j.jpsychires.2017.10.015.
records.protocolTakeaway: Use as a practical dose anchor, not as definitive treatment evidence.

records.title: Amber lenses to block blue light and improve sleep: a randomized trial
records.citation: Burkhart K, Phelps JR. Amber lenses to block blue light and improve sleep: a randomized trial. Chronobiol Int. 2009;26(8):1602-1612. doi:10.3109/07420520903523719.
records.protocolTakeaway: Supports a bounded evening test but does not overcome the small-study and subjective-outcome limitations.

records.title: Effect of evening blue light blocking glasses on subjective and objective sleep in healthy adults: a randomized control trial
records.citation: Bigalke JA, et al. Effect of evening blue light blocking glasses on subjective and objective sleep in healthy adults: a randomized control trial. Sleep Health. 2021;7(4):485-490. doi:10.1016/j.sleh.2021.02.004.
records.protocolTakeaway: Low-symptom users may see little or no objective signal.

records.title: A randomized controlled trial on the effects of blue-blocking glasses compared to partial blue-blockers on sleep outcomes in the third trimester of pregnancy
records.citation: Liset R, et al. A randomized controlled trial on the effects of blue-blocking glasses compared to partial blue-blockers on sleep outcomes in the third trimester of pregnancy. PLoS One. 2022;17(1):e0262799. doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0262799.
records.protocolTakeaway: Pregnancy is an adjacent supervised variant; do not use this as a general adult protocol proof.

records.title: A randomized controlled trial on the effect of blue-blocking glasses compared to partial blue-blockers on melatonin profile among nulliparous women in third trimester of the pregnancy
records.journal: Neurobiology of Sleep and Circadian Rhythms
records.citation: Liset R, et al. A randomized controlled trial on the effect of blue-blocking glasses compared to partial blue-blockers on melatonin profile among nulliparous women in third trimester of the pregnancy. Neurobiol Sleep Circadian Rhythms. 2021;12:100074. doi:10.1016/j.nbscr.2021.100074.
records.protocolTakeaway: Do not equate melatonin movement with reliable sleep improvement.

records.title: Use of Actigraphy for the Evaluation of Sleep Disorders and Circadian Rhythm Sleep-Wake Disorders: An American Academy of Sleep Medicine Clinical Practice Guideline
records.citation: Smith MT, et al. Use of Actigraphy for the Evaluation of Sleep Disorders and Circadian Rhythm Sleep-Wake Disorders: An American Academy of Sleep Medicine Clinical Practice Guideline. J Clin Sleep Med. 2018;14(7):1231-1237. doi:10.5664/jcsm.7230.
records.protocolTakeaway: Use wearable estimates as trend proxies and pair them with subjective sleep-onset logging.

records.title: The Ottawa sunglasses at night study: A randomized controlled trial of blue-blocking glasses for mania
records.citation: Fiedorowicz JG, et al. The Ottawa sunglasses at night study: A randomized controlled trial of blue-blocking glasses for mania. J Affect Disord. 2026;398:120910. doi:10.1016/j.jad.2025.120910.
records.protocolTakeaway: Mood-disorder use needs clinician oversight and should not be folded into Murph’s general wellness protocol.
